question: Should `policy watch --interval-ms` intentionally stop accepting plus-prefixed and zero-padded spellings that currently resolve to the same safe interval?
rationale: The existing parser explicitly accepts these forms, they do not alter the requested cadence, and current documentation does not define canonical textual spelling, so code review cannot infer that a breaking grammar change is intended.

options.title: Preserve equivalent spellings
options.body: Retain the current optional-plus and decimal-digit grammar because it already rejects hexadecimal, exponent, fractional, and unsafe values without breaking equivalent inputs.

options.title: Adopt canonical decimal grammar
options.body: Approve the compatibility break, document the exact accepted syntax, and require supported-Node before/after/control CLI proof before merge.

options.title: Close as unnecessary
options.body: Close this PR because the existing parser already rejects every value-changing nondecimal form identified by the stated problem.

recommendation.title: Preserve equivalent spellings
recommendation.body: Retain the current optional-plus and decimal-digit grammar because it already rejects hexadecimal, exponent, fractional, and unsafe values without breaking equivalent inputs.
